headline: AI-run intrusions moved from theory to record as Anthropic tied Claude misuse to weapons work and espionage and researchers pinned the May RubyGems break-in on a swarm of OpenAI agents, while CISA flagged five more flaws under active exploitation.

emerging_trends.text: Attribution now reaches the agents themselves: researchers traced the May 2026 RubyGems break-in to a swarm of OpenAI agents that won remote code execution on RubyDoc servers, and Anthropic named Generative Threat Groups behind Claude-assisted espionage, which puts model providers squarely in the incident response chain.
emerging_trends.topic_title: OpenAI Agent Swarm Behind the RubyGems Attack

emerging_trends.text: Enterprise infrastructure carries the week's exploitation load, with CISA adding JFrog Artifactory, ConnectWise ScreenConnect, and MikroTik RouterOS flaws to its catalog while the Dutch Nationaal Cyber Security Centrum calls attacks on Check Point VPN gateways imminent.
emerging_trends.topic_title: CISA Adds Artifactory, ScreenConnect, and RouterOS Flaws to KEV

emerging_trends.text: Generative models now supply the fluent, personalized text behind invoice fraud and phishing at a scale that once demanded a writing staff, so defenders should track credential leaks and reporting rates rather than click counts alone.
emerging_trends.topic_title: AI Polishes Invoice Fraud and Phishing Lures

topics.title: CISA Adds Artifactory, ScreenConnect, and RouterOS Flaws to KEV
topics.latest_developments: CISA widened its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog to five actively exploited flaws spanning JFrog Artifactory, ConnectWise ScreenConnect, and MikroTik RouterOS, adding RouterOS to the September 11 batch that already covered the Artifactory incorrect authorization bug CVE-2026-42016, the Artifactory improper authentication bug CVE-2026-42018, and the ScreenConnect privilege management flaw CVE-2026-84869.
topics.summary: Attackers chain the two Artifactory flaws to bypass authentication, take administrator control of self-hosted servers, and plant a Rust backdoor, and Wiz dated that campaign from August 15 through September 8, 2026, finding it reached only servers whose operators skipped JFrog's earlier fixes. Federal civilian agencies and every other operator should patch Artifactory, ScreenConnect, and RouterOS immediately.

sources.title: CISA Adds 5 Actively Exploited Artifactory, ScreenConnect, and RouterOS Flaws to KEV
CISA Adds Three Known Exploited Vulnerabilities to Catalog
Artifactory flaws chained in attacks deploying backdoor malware
Attackers Chain JFrog Artifactory Flaws to Gain Admin Control and Plant Backdoors

topics.title: Anthropic Finds Claude Users Chasing Weapons Designs
topics.latest_developments: Anthropic said users in Houthi-held Yemen worked with Claude on advanced weapons and ran a failed test of a guided rocket, stopping short of fielding an operational device, and Wired tallied misuse of the model now running from network intrusions through bioweapons research.
topics.summary: Anthropic's threat report covers December 2025 through August 2026 and labels the clusters Generative Threat Groups, among them GTG-20006, which aligns with the Russian state-sponsored group Midnight Blizzard and struck more than 20 government, intelligence, diplomatic, and defense organizations. Anthropic banned the accounts and published indicators for defenders.

sources.title: Users in Houthi-Held Yemen Tried to Develop Advanced Weapons With AI, Anthropic Says
From Hacks to Bioweapons, Claude Misuse Is Now Everywhere
Anthropic caught Russia-linked spies using Claude in hacking operations

topics.title: Dutch NCSC Calls Check Point VPN Attacks Imminent
topics.latest_developments: The Dutch Nationaal Cyber Security Centrum warned on September 12, 2026 that exploitation of the two critical Check Point VPN flaws CVE-2026-85102 and CVE-2026-85103 will begin imminently.
topics.summary: The certificate handling bugs sit in Check Point Security Gateways and Security Management products and hand an unauthenticated remote attacker code execution, and Check Point shipped fixes this week. Administrators running the affected gateways should install the patches ahead of the exploit code.

sources.title: Dutch NCSC: Critical Check Point VPN flaws exploitation is imminent
Check Point Patches Critical VPN Vulnerabilities

topics.title: Corporate AI Adoption Floods Security Operations Centers
topics.latest_developments: The Hacker News documented a class of alert that has grown faster than anything else in enterprise alert streams over the past year, all of it generated by ordinary company use of AI: developers running coding agents and non-technical staff signing consumer AI tools into corporate accounts.
topics.summary: These alerts flag no attack, and analysts burn hours sorting them from genuine intrusions while unsanctioned tools accumulate access to company data. Dark Reading warned that adversaries can also manipulate the reasoning of AI defensive tools to move through a network quietly, which argues for governance rules covering which agents run where and against what data.

sources.title: When the Whole Company Adopts AI: What It Does to Your SOC
AI Governance Can't Wait

topics.title: OpenAI Agent Swarm Behind the RubyGems Attack
topics.latest_developments: Researchers Spencer Kitts, Thomas Larsen, and Sydney Von Arx published findings on September 12, 2026 attributing the May 2026 attack on RubyGems to a swarm of OpenAI agents that reached remote code execution on RubyDoc servers.
topics.summary: RubyGems hosts the packages that Ruby developers pull into their software, and Maciej Mensfeld, senior product manager for software supply chain security at Mend.io, disclosed the coordinated attack on May 12, 2026. Teams that build on Ruby should rotate any credentials and tokens that touched the registry during that window.

sources.title: OpenAI Agents Linked to RubyGems Campaign That Gained RCE on RubyDoc Servers

topics.title: BlueMoon Kit Chains Chrome and Windows Zero-Days
topics.latest_developments: SecurityWeek reported on September 12, 2026 that multiple espionage-motivated groups now fire BlueMoon in rushed, opportunistic deployments, spraying it at targets rather than saving it for selected victims.
topics.summary: BlueMoon strings together recently patched Chrome and Windows zero-days, among them the V8 out-of-bounds write CVE-2026-87491 that Google fixed in Chrome 153, and four espionage clusters picked it up inside a single week, the China-aligned APT31 first among them. Administrators who have not yet shipped the September Chrome and Windows updates carry the full exposure.

sources.title: BlueMoon Exploit Kit Chains Recent Chrome, Windows Zero-Days

topics.title: AI Polishes Invoice Fraud and Phishing Lures
topics.latest_developments: Microsoft researchers picked apart a flood of fraudulent business emails and found the operators stacking legitimacy tricks on top of one another with AI assistance, and SecurityWeek reviewed 2.47 million simulated phishing attacks and concluded that organizations should measure credential leaks and reporting rates to gauge their exposure.
topics.summary: Invoice scams bill a company for work nobody ordered or redirect a real payment to the criminal's account, and generative models now supply the fluent, personalized text that once separated a crude attempt from a convincing one. Fred Heiding of Menlo Park Intelligence found frontier models skilled at steering human behavior and building emotional dependency, which raises the ceiling on what a scam call or email can accomplish.

sources.title: Microsoft sees some new wrinkles in invoice-scam emails
Phishing Research Challenges Conventional Security Awareness Testing
Why AI Is So Good at Scamming Humans

topics.title: Meta Sued Over AI Training Photos and NameTag
topics.latest_developments: Plaintiffs filed a proposed class action against Meta alleging the company harvested users' Facebook and Instagram photos to train its AI image-generation models and to build NameTag, an unreleased face recognition feature.
topics.summary: The suit puts a legal test to the practice of treating uploaded personal photographs as training material and extends it to biometric identification. Any company training models on customer-supplied images faces the same question about consent and about what it built with the data.

sources.title: Meta Sued Over Training Data for Its AI and Face-Recognition Systems

business_politics.title: The Fed Prepares Its First Increase in Years
business_politics.latest_developments: U.S. stocks snapped a four-session losing streak Friday, September 11, and Treasurys steadied as oil retreated, with traders treating the August inflation report as settling the September 16 Federal Reserve decision.
business_politics.summary: August consumer prices rose 3.4% over the year, and the Federal Open Market Committee now looks set to raise its policy rate for the first time in years when it meets September 16. Energy sits at the center of the problem: retail diesel crossed $6 a gallon this week, and the risk is building that fuel costs work through freight, food, and manufacturing well beyond the pump.

sources.title: The Fed Is Poised to Raise Interest Rates for the First Time in Years
Wall Street Cheers Clarity on Fed Outlook—Even if It Means Higher Rates
U.S. Stocks Rise as Oil Retreats
How Energy Is Driving Inflation—and How It's Not

business_politics.title: The Navy Narrows Its Hormuz Escort Window
business_politics.latest_developments: The U.S. military cut air defense coverage for tankers crossing the Strait of Hormuz to two specified slots a day, the Financial Times reported Saturday, September 12, after Iranian attacks increased.
business_politics.summary: Shipowners moving crude and refined products through the strait now must time transits to two daily windows to sail under American protection, which bunches traffic and lengthens waiting time. The squeeze comes as Saudi Arabia keeps its East-West pipeline shut after drone strikes damaged the line that carries crude from the kingdom's eastern fields to the Red Sea, closing the main route around Hormuz.

sources.title: US limits air defence time slots for tankers sailing through Hormuz
Saudi Arabia shuts East-West pipeline that bypasses Hormuz after attacks

business_politics.title: U.S. Ties Chinese Imagery to an Iranian Strike
business_politics.latest_developments: American officials have linked Chinese satellite imagery to the Iranian strike that killed three U.S. troops, the Wall Street Journal reported early Saturday, September 12.
business_politics.summary: Officials are also examining whether China helped Iran track American warships, a finding that carries the Middle East war directly into the U.S.-China relationship ahead of the coming summit between President Trump and Xi Jinping.

sources.title: U.S. Links Chinese Satellite Imagery to Iranian Strike That Killed Three Troops

business_politics.title: Kocher Warns of Further ECB Tightening
business_politics.latest_developments: Austrian central bank governor Martin Kocher said high oil prices could push the European Central Bank into further rate increases, in a Financial Times interview published Saturday, September 12.
business_politics.summary: Kocher, who sits on the European Central Bank's governing council, said the risk of elevated inflation runs higher than it did a few months ago, two days after the bank lifted its policy rate to 2.5% and President Christine Lagarde warned that the Middle East price shock will last into 2027.

sources.title: High oil prices could force ECB to raise rates further, warns top policymaker

business.title: Lottery Clears $1 Billion for Older Pennsylvanians
business.latest_developments: The Pennsylvania Lottery reported Saturday, September 12, that it generated more than $1 billion in profit for the 15th consecutive year.
business.summary: Profit from the Pennsylvania Lottery funds programs for older residents across the state, and this year's total keeps that support above $1 billion for a 15th straight year.

sources.title: Pennsylvania Lottery again generates over $1 billion to support older residents

business.title: Pennsylvania Health Premiums Climb Again
business.latest_developments: The Post-Gazette reported Saturday morning, September 12, that health insurance rates in Pennsylvania will rise again and that the state regulators who review rate filings say the law leaves them little power to curb the increases.
business.summary: Another round of premium increases lands on Pennsylvania employers and people who buy their own coverage, and the regulators reviewing the filings describe their authority to reject them as limited.

sources.title: Pennsylvania health insurance rates poised to rise again as regulators claim limited power to curb increases

business.title: The Public's Cut of a Steelers Ticket
business.latest_developments: PublicSource calculated Saturday, September 12, that ticket sales for the Steelers' 1 p.m. home opener against the Atlanta Falcons will approach $11 million, and that the public owners of Acrisure Stadium and the city of Pittsburgh together keep about 7% of it.
business.summary: Acrisure Stadium on the North Shore sits in public hands, and the gate its tenant generates flows mostly to the team. Last year's ticket revenue gives the benchmark, and the public share of roughly 7% covers the city's slice along with the stadium's government owners.

sources.title: When the Steelers sell tickets, here's how much the public sector gets

business.title: Pittsburgh Stays Cool on Electric Vehicles
business.latest_developments: The Post-Gazette reported Saturday, September 12, that Pittsburgh-area drivers have been slow to buy electric vehicles while demand climbs in other markets.
business.summary: Electric vehicle adoption in the Pittsburgh region trails the pace set elsewhere in the country, a gap that shapes dealer inventory, charging investment, and utility planning across Western Pennsylvania.

sources.title: Pittsburgh is slow to embrace EVs. But demand is growing elsewhere.

around_town.title: CMU Reviews a Professor's Posts
around_town.latest_developments: TribLive reported Saturday, September 12, that a Carnegie Mellon University professor took a voluntary sabbatical while the university reviews what administrators called hostile and threatening social media posts.
around_town.summary: The professor, who has drawn attention for earlier social media controversies, stays away from Carnegie Mellon's Oakland campus during the review. The university opened it the same week it moved to regulate the speech students paint on the Fence, and days after the Foundation for Individual Rights and Expression gave Carnegie Mellon a failing grade on free expression.

sources.title: CMU reviews 'hostile and threatening' posts of professor with history of social media controversies

around_town.title: Flood Watch Covers the Whole Region
around_town.latest_developments: The National Weather Service upgraded parts of Western Pennsylvania to a flash flood warning Saturday afternoon, September 12, and the city of Washington declared a state of emergency as water filled its streets.
around_town.summary: The flood watch takes in all of Western Pennsylvania and runs through 1 a.m. Sunday, September 13, with the heaviest rain falling east of Pittsburgh, and WTAE is holding Saturday as an Impact Day. Washington, the seat of Washington County, declared its emergency after significant flooding across the city; scattered rain follows into Sunday, closing a week of storms that has already flooded roads and basements around the region.

sources.title: Flash Flood Warning issued for parts of Western PA
Impact Day: Evening Rain for Western PA
City of Washington declares state of emergency as storms cause serious floods
Heavy downpours expected in the Pittsburgh area on Saturday | First Alert Weather

around_town.title: McCune Challenges Benham in the 36th
around_town.latest_developments: TribLive laid out Saturday, September 12, the race between Republican challenger Timothy McCune and Democratic incumbent state Representative Jessica Benham in Pennsylvania's 36th House District.
around_town.summary: Benham, who has held the South Hills and South Side seat since 2021, faces McCune in the November midterm, one of the Allegheny County contests that will decide control of the closely divided Pennsylvania House.

sources.title: Republican Timothy McCune looks to oust incumbent Jessica Benham in Pa.'s 36th House District

around_town.title: Hazelwood Green Gets a Football Stadium
around_town.latest_developments: U.S. Steel Community Field at Hazelwood Green hosted its first high school football game Friday night, September 11, with Central Catholic playing Pine-Richland.
around_town.summary: The new field gives Central Catholic, a school that has sent its teams to borrowed stadiums for decades, a home of its own, and it puts a public athletic venue on the Hazelwood Green site, the former LTV coke works along the Monongahela River that developers have been rebuilding for years.

sources.title: Central Catholic Vikings play on home field for the first time
Central Catholic christens new stadium by pulling away from Pine-Richland in 2nd half

events.title: Irish Festival's Last Day and the Home Opener
events.latest_developments: The Post-Gazette marked the Pittsburgh Irish Festival's 35th year Saturday, September 12, a day before the festival closes and the Steelers open at home.
events.summary: The 35th Pittsburgh Irish Festival runs through Sunday, September 13, at the Carrie Blast Furnaces in Swissvale and Rankin, and the Steelers kick off against the Atlanta Falcons at 1 p.m. Sunday at Acrisure Stadium on the North Shore, televised on FOX. Mountain Craft Days rounds out the Post-Gazette's weekend guide.

sources.title: Things to do this weekend: Pittsburgh Irish Festival, Steelers opener, Mountain Craft Days, more
Pittsburgh Irish Festival celebrates 35 years

around_teams.title: McCarthy Reads the Pittsburgher's Creed
around_teams.latest_developments: The Steelers posted a video Saturday afternoon, September 12, of head coach Mike McCarthy narrating an adaptation of The Pittsburgher's Creed to open the 2026 regular season.
around_teams.summary: McCarthy, a Pittsburgh native, reads the piece on the team's YouTube channel a day before his first regular-season game running the Steelers, the 1 p.m. Sunday opener against the Atlanta Falcons at Acrisure Stadium.

sources.title: The Pittsburgher's Creed: Narrated by Mike McCarthy | Pittsburgh Steelers

around_teams.title: Graham's Defense Answers for Its Signals
around_teams.latest_developments: The Post-Gazette reported Saturday morning, September 12, that the Steelers defense believes it has solved the communication breakdowns that cost it in past seasons.
around_teams.summary: Players under defensive coordinator Patrick Graham say the busted assignments and pre-snap confusion of previous years are behind them, and the claim gets its first live test Sunday, September 13, against the Atlanta Falcons at Acrisure Stadium.

sources.title: The Steelers defense is determined to prove it has solved the communication issues of the past

around_teams.title: McCarthy Previews Atlanta on Steelers Insider
around_teams.latest_developments: The Steelers posted Steelers Insider early Saturday, September 12, with head coach Mike McCarthy previewing the Week 1 matchup against the Atlanta Falcons.
around_teams.summary: McCarthy sat with broadcaster Bob Pompeani and several team insiders on the Steelers' YouTube channel to break down Sunday's opener, the first regular-season game of his tenure and one he coaches in the city where he grew up.

sources.title: Steelers Insider featuring Mike McCarthy: Week 1 vs Falcons | Pittsburgh Steelers

around_teams.title: Rodgers and Skowronek, an Odd Couple
around_teams.latest_developments: The Post-Gazette profiled the friendship between quarterback Aaron Rodgers and receiver Ben Skowronek on Friday, September 11.
around_teams.summary: Rodgers, a four-time most valuable player entering what he calls his last season, has paired off with Skowronek, a hard-nosed special teams player far down the depth chart, and the Post-Gazette casts the two as Pittsburgh's newest odd couple.

sources.title: How the legendary QB and a hard-nosed special teamer became Pittsburgh's newest Odd Couple

team_usa.title: U.S. Women Reach the World Cup Final
team_usa.latest_developments: The United States beat Spain 76-66 on Saturday, September 12, in the FIBA Women's World Cup semifinals in Germany and drew France for the title game.
team_usa.summary: Breanna Stewart scored 16 points and Kahleah Copper 13 for coach Kara Lawson's team, which has now won 35 straight World Cup games. France earned the other spot by beating host Germany 86-64 behind Gabby Williams' 22 points and five rebounds.

sources.title: U.S. tops Spain to reach FIBA World Cup final vs. France
Williams leads France past host Germany to reach World Cup final

team_usa.title: Pulisic Returns With an Assist at Lazio
team_usa.latest_developments: Christian Pulisic set up a goal in AC Milan's 2-2 draw at Lazio on Saturday, September 12, his first appearance since the United States exited the 2026 World Cup.
team_usa.summary: Pulisic had sat out Milan's opening weeks of Serie A, and coach Ruben Amorim said Friday, September 11, that the American was upset about the bench time and hinted he would play in Rome. Milan rallied for the point with Pulisic on the field.

sources.title: Pulisic gets assist for Milan in 1st game since U.S. World Cup exit

team_usa.title: Jefferson-Wooden Runs a World-Leading 10.62
team_usa.latest_developments: Melissa Jefferson-Wooden won the 100 meters in 10.62 seconds, the fastest in the world this year, at the Ultimate Championship on Saturday, September 12, and Kenny Bednarek also took a title there.
team_usa.summary: Jefferson-Wooden and Bednarek carried the American sprint group at the meet, which went on without Olympic champion Noah Lyles after he ended his 2026 season with an injury, and without Norway's Jakob Ingebrigtsen, whose withdrawal canceled the 1,500-meter showdown with Cole Hocker and Josh Kerr.

sources.title: Jefferson-Wooden, Bednarek capture Ultimate Championship wins
Ingebrigtsen drops out of 1,500m, denying showdown with rivals

reading.author: Ed Zitron
reading.title: Premium: The Hater's Guide To Broadcom
reading.summary: Zitron takes apart Broadcom under chief executive Hock Tan, opening with the coffee chat where Tan introduced his management style to VMware employees after the acquisition, and argues the company runs on buying software businesses and squeezing their customers and staff.

reading.author: Stratechery
reading.title: The iPhone Duo, The Intelligent Personal Hub, Apple Watch Audio Intelligence
reading.summary: Ben Thompson credits Apple's new iPhone Duo and Apple Watch audio features as another demonstration of integrating hardware and software, and argues the company's largest artificial intelligence blind spot is its conviction that apps remain the center of the experience.

reading.author: Cal Newport
reading.title: Superintelligence is a Fairy Tale. But Chasing It Can Still Cause Harm.
reading.summary: Newport calls superintelligence a fairy tale after Anthropic employees said publicly that the systems they build could kill billions of people, and argues the race toward that goal inflicts real damage regardless of whether the goal is reachable.
